question.text: A mutual fund equity-oriented scheme has an AUM of Rs. 1,000 crore. As per SEBI's slab structure for equity-oriented schemes, the maximum TER is 2.25% on the first Rs. 500 crore, 2.00% on the next Rs. 250 crore, and 1.75% on the next Rs. 250 crore. What is the maximum permissible TER expense for the first Rs. 1,000 crore of AUM?

explanation.text: The Logic: TER is applied in slabs. For the first Rs. 500 crore: Rs. 500 crore x 2.25% = Rs. 11.25 crore. For the next Rs. 250 crore: Rs. 250 crore x 2.00% = Rs. 5.00 crore. For the next Rs. 250 crore: Rs. 250 crore x 1.75% = Rs. 4.375 crore. Total for Rs. 1,000 crore = Rs. 11.25 + Rs. 5.00 + Rs. 4.375 = Rs. 20.625 crore. The Trap: Rs. 22.50 crore applies 2.25% on the entire Rs. 1,000 crore — ignoring the slab structure. Rs. 21.25 crore wrongly applies 2.00% to the entire next Rs. 500 crore, ignoring that the 2.00% slab covers only Rs. 250 crore and the next Rs. 250 crore is at 1.75%. Rs. 20.00 crore applies 2.00% flat on Rs. 1,000 crore. Note: SEBI's TER slab structure for equity-oriented schemes uses progressively lower percentages for larger AUM tranches, so the effective TER falls as AUM rises.
